benchmarks.label: Payment terms
benchmarks.market_norm: Net 30
benchmarks.note: Net 15 or upfront prepayment is below market for an annual commitment. Prepayment should buy a discount of at least 5%.

benchmarks.label: Annual price uplift cap
benchmarks.market_norm: 3-5% or CPI, whichever is lower
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: CPI capped at 3%, first renewal flat
benchmarks.note: Uncapped uplift is the single most common hidden cost in SaaS. A 7% annual uplift nearly doubles spend over 10 years.

benchmarks.label: Termination for convenience
benchmarks.market_norm: 30-60 days written notice at term end
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 30 days any time, pro-rata refund
benchmarks.note: No termination-for-convenience right at all means you are locked in for the full term regardless of performance.

benchmarks.label: Auto-renewal window
benchmarks.market_norm: Auto-renews with a 30-day opt-out window
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Opt-in renewal, or 90-day reminder from the vendor
benchmarks.note: A 90-day opt-out window on a 12-month term means you must decide before you have even used three quarters of the service.

benchmarks.label: Liability cap
benchmarks.market_norm: 12 months of fees paid
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 12 months of fees, uncapped for data breach, IP infringement and wilful misconduct
benchmarks.note: A cap set at 3 months of fees, or at the fees paid in the month of the incident, is well below market.

benchmarks.label: Uptime SLA and service credits
benchmarks.market_norm: 99.9% uptime, 10% monthly credit on breach
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 99.95% uptime, escalating credits, termination right after repeated breach
benchmarks.note: Credits that must be claimed by the customer within 30 days are usually never claimed. Ask for automatic credits.

benchmarks.label: Data export and exit assistance
benchmarks.market_norm: Data returned in a standard format within 30 days of termination
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Self-serve export at any time, 90-day post-termination access window
benchmarks.note: Charging a fee for data export at exit is a lock-in tactic and is negotiable in almost every deal.

benchmarks.label: Payment terms
benchmarks.market_norm: Net 30 on invoice, monthly in arrears
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Net 45 in arrears, tied to accepted deliverables
benchmarks.note: Paying in advance for unperformed work removes all of your leverage if delivery slips.

benchmarks.label: Rate card and annual rate increases
benchmarks.market_norm: Rates fixed for 12 months, then CPI
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Rates fixed for the whole engagement, volume-tiered discounts
benchmarks.note: Ask for a blended rate rather than per-grade rates; it stops the supplier substituting expensive seniors into routine work.

benchmarks.label: Change control and scope creep
benchmarks.market_norm: Written change order required, priced before work starts
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Change orders priced at the original rate card, with a not-to-exceed cap
benchmarks.note: Without a not-to-exceed cap, a time-and-materials engagement has no ceiling.

benchmarks.label: Deliverable acceptance
benchmarks.market_norm: 10 business days to accept or reject in writing
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 15 business days, deemed rejected if silent, rework at supplier cost
benchmarks.note: Watch for 'deemed accepted if no response' clauses paired with a short window.

benchmarks.label: Key personnel continuity
benchmarks.market_norm: Named leads cannot be replaced without customer consent
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Named leads locked for the engagement, replacements matched on seniority at no extra cost
benchmarks.note: The team who pitched is often not the team who delivers. Name them in the contract.

benchmarks.label: IP ownership of deliverables
benchmarks.market_norm: Customer owns bespoke deliverables, supplier keeps pre-existing IP
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Customer owns deliverables plus a perpetual licence to embedded supplier IP
benchmarks.note: If the supplier retains ownership of work you paid for, you cannot maintain it without them.

benchmarks.label: Non-solicitation of staff
benchmarks.market_norm: Mutual, 6-12 months after engagement ends
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Mutual, 6 months, with a buy-out fee option
benchmarks.note: One-sided non-solicits that only bind the customer are common and are usually conceded when challenged.

benchmarks.label: Payment terms
benchmarks.market_norm: Net 30 from invoice date
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Net 45-60, with disputed lines not delaying payment of the rest
benchmarks.note: Quick-pay discounts of 1-2% for Net 10 are standard and worth modelling against your cost of capital.

benchmarks.label: Fuel surcharge mechanism
benchmarks.market_norm: Indexed to a published national fuel index, reviewed monthly
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Published index, capped, with a floor that passes savings back when fuel falls
benchmarks.note: Surcharges that only ratchet upward and never fall are the classic hidden cost in freight contracts.

benchmarks.label: Accessorial and ancillary charges
benchmarks.market_norm: Published accessorial schedule fixed for the term
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Closed list of accessorials; anything not listed cannot be charged
benchmarks.note: Open-ended accessorial schedules the supplier can amend at will routinely add 10-20% to landed cost.

benchmarks.label: Annual rate review
benchmarks.market_norm: Annual review indexed to CPI or a transport cost index
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Annual review capped at CPI, with a benchmarking right against market rates
benchmarks.note: A benchmarking clause lets you test rates mid-term without terminating.

benchmarks.label: Minimum volume commitment
benchmarks.market_norm: No minimum, or a soft target with no penalty
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: No committed minimum; discounts tiered on actual volume
benchmarks.note: Committed minimums with shortfall penalties transfer demand risk from the carrier to you.

benchmarks.label: Cargo loss and damage liability
benchmarks.market_norm: Standard carrier liability per applicable convention
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Declared value coverage for high-value lanes, agreed claims turnaround
benchmarks.note: Check the claims notification window; 7-day windows are easy to miss and void the claim.

benchmarks.label: On-time performance SLA
benchmarks.market_norm: 95% on-time delivery measured monthly
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 97% on-time, service credits, termination right on sustained failure
benchmarks.note: An SLA with no financial consequence is a target, not a service level.

benchmarks.label: Payment terms
benchmarks.market_norm: Net 30-45 from delivery
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Net 60 from receipt and acceptance of goods
benchmarks.note: Anchor payment to acceptance, not to despatch, so defective shipments do not become your financing problem.

benchmarks.label: Raw material price adjustment
benchmarks.market_norm: Indexed to a published commodity index, reviewed quarterly
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Symmetric index with a cap and a collar, passing decreases back
benchmarks.note: Asymmetric pass-through clauses that only move upward are widespread and highly negotiable.

benchmarks.label: Minimum order quantity / take-or-pay
benchmarks.market_norm: MOQ per order, no annual take-or-pay
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Rolling forecast with a non-binding horizon beyond 90 days
benchmarks.note: Take-or-pay commitments are the largest hidden liability in supply agreements.

benchmarks.label: Lead time and delivery performance
benchmarks.market_norm: Agreed lead time, 95% on-time-in-full
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Committed lead time with liquidated damages for late delivery
benchmarks.note: Suppliers often accept OTIF measurement but resist any financial consequence. Push for both.

benchmarks.label: Quality warranty period
benchmarks.market_norm: 12 months from delivery
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 24 months from commissioning, plus epidemic failure protection
benchmarks.note: Warranties that run from despatch rather than commissioning quietly shorten your cover.

benchmarks.label: Tooling and equipment ownership
benchmarks.market_norm: Customer owns tooling it paid for
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Customer owns tooling with a right of immediate physical retrieval
benchmarks.note: Owning tooling on paper is worthless without an enforceable right to collect it from the supplier's floor.

benchmarks.label: Termination for convenience
benchmarks.market_norm: 90 days written notice
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 60 days, liability limited to finished goods and committed raw material
benchmarks.note: Check what you owe on termination; open-ended reimbursement of supplier costs is a blank cheque.

benchmarks.label: Contractor mark-up
benchmarks.market_norm: 18-28% over pay rate for standard roles
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 15-20%, tiered down as volume rises
benchmarks.note: Mark-up should be transparent and separately stated. Bundled all-in rates hide the margin.

benchmarks.label: Permanent placement fee
benchmarks.market_norm: 18-22% of first-year salary
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 15% with volume rebates, capped in absolute terms for senior hires
benchmarks.note: A percentage fee with no absolute cap is expensive on executive hires.

benchmarks.label: Replacement guarantee / rebate
benchmarks.market_norm: Sliding rebate over 12 weeks
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Free replacement within 12 weeks, then sliding rebate to 6 months
benchmarks.note: Check whether the rebate is cash back or a credit note. Credit notes are worth far less.

benchmarks.label: Contractor-to-permanent conversion fee
benchmarks.market_norm: Sliding fee, reaching zero after 12 months of engagement
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Zero fee after 6 months of continuous engagement
benchmarks.note: Flat conversion fees that never taper are a hidden penalty for hiring people who work out well.

benchmarks.label: Payment terms
benchmarks.market_norm: Net 30 from timesheet approval
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Net 45 from consolidated monthly self-bill
benchmarks.note: Weekly invoicing on Net 7 terms is common in staffing and is usually negotiable to monthly.

benchmarks.label: Exclusivity / preferred supplier lock-in
benchmarks.market_norm: Non-exclusive preferred supplier status
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Non-exclusive, with the right to run a panel
benchmarks.note: Exclusivity removes your ability to price-test. Rarely worth the discount offered for it.

benchmarks.label: Annual rate increases
benchmarks.market_norm: Reviewed annually, indexed to wage inflation
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Mark-up fixed for the term; only the underlying pay rate moves
benchmarks.note: Insist that annual increases apply to pay rate only, not to the agency's mark-up percentage.

benchmarks.label: Payment terms
benchmarks.market_norm: Monthly valuation, Net 30 from certification
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Net 45 from certification, with agreed valuation dates
benchmarks.note: Check local prompt-payment legislation before agreeing anything longer than statute allows.

benchmarks.label: Retention
benchmarks.market_norm: 5% retention, half released at practical completion
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 5% retention, balance released 12 months after practical completion
benchmarks.note: Retention is your main leverage over defect rectification. Do not trade it away for a small discount.

benchmarks.label: Variations and change orders
benchmarks.market_norm: Priced from the contract rate schedule before work starts
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Rate schedule fixed for the project, dayworks capped
benchmarks.note: Variations priced after the fact, at rates set by the contractor, are where project budgets die.

benchmarks.label: Delay liquidated damages
benchmarks.market_norm: 0.1-0.5% of contract value per week, capped at 5-10%
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Genuine pre-estimate of loss, capped at 10%
benchmarks.note: A cap that is too low makes late delivery cheaper for the contractor than mobilising more labour.

benchmarks.label: Extension of time grounds
benchmarks.market_norm: Relief for client-caused delay and defined force majeure
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Closed list of relief events, notice required within 14 days
benchmarks.note: Open-ended 'any cause beyond the contractor's control' wording will absorb almost every delay.

benchmarks.label: Defects liability period
benchmarks.market_norm: 12 months from practical completion
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 24 months, with latent defect cover backed by collateral warranties
benchmarks.note: Ask who carries the defect risk after the period expires and whether warranties are assignable.

benchmarks.label: Insurance and performance bonds
benchmarks.market_norm: Performance bond at 10% of contract value
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: On-demand bond at 10%, plus parent company guarantee
benchmarks.note: A conditional bond is much harder to call than an on-demand one. The difference matters when it matters.

benchmarks.label: Payment terms
benchmarks.market_norm: Net 30
benchmarks.note: Shorter terms than Net 30 should be traded for a discount, not conceded for free.

benchmarks.label: Annual price increase
benchmarks.market_norm: CPI, or 3-5%
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: CPI capped at 3%, first year flat
benchmarks.note: Uncapped or supplier-discretion price increases are the most common hidden cost in any contract.

benchmarks.label: Termination for convenience
benchmarks.market_norm: 30-90 days written notice
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 30 days, no early termination charge
benchmarks.note: Also check the exit costs; a short notice period is worthless if leaving triggers a large fee.

benchmarks.label: Auto-renewal
benchmarks.market_norm: Auto-renews with a 30-day opt-out window
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Opt-in renewal with a written reminder before the window opens
benchmarks.note: Long opt-out windows combined with automatic renewal are how contracts silently extend for another full term.

benchmarks.label: Liability cap
benchmarks.market_norm: 12 months of fees paid
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: 12 months of fees, with carve-outs for breach of confidentiality and wilful misconduct
benchmarks.note: A mutual cap is standard. A cap that protects only the supplier is not.

benchmarks.label: Indemnities
benchmarks.market_norm: Mutual indemnities for third-party claims
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Supplier indemnifies for IP infringement and data breach, mutual otherwise
benchmarks.note: Read indemnities alongside the liability cap; an indemnity carved out of the cap is unlimited exposure.

benchmarks.label: Assignment and change of control
benchmarks.market_norm: Neither party may assign without consent, not unreasonably withheld
benchmarks.buyer_favourable: Customer may assign within its group freely; supplier change of control gives a termination right
benchmarks.note: Without a change-of-control right you can end up contracted to your supplier's acquirer, possibly a competitor.
